w:r.w:t: Property Sync – A MERN-Based Property Management System

Managing rental properties manually is fragmented, error-prone, and time-consuming. Property owners struggle to track multiple units, coordinate with tenants, collect rent, and maintain lease documents across disparate tools. Tenants, on the other hand, lack a unified digital portal to view their lease agreements, pay rent online, and communicate with their landlords. Traditional systems do not provide real-time visibility for administrators who need cross-platform oversight of users, properties, and payments.

stack MERN application with three role-based portals Admin, Owner, and Tenant that centralizes every aspect of property management. Owners can list properties, upload photos, assign tenants, and generate PDF lease agreements. Tenants can browse available listings, sign leases, and pay rent securely via Stripe. Administrators have a live dashboard with charts, user management, and automated downloadable reports. Email notifications are dispatched via SendGrid for key events such as new listings and lease changes.

The frontend is split into three independent Create React App (CRA) applications: admin-frontend, owner-frontend, and tenant-frontend. Each follows the same layered hierarchy:
pages/ – route-level page components (e.g., DashboardPage, PropertiesPage)
components/ – reusable UI units grouped by domain (Auth/, Properties/, Dashboard/, Sidebar/, Topbar/)
layout/ – MainLayout wrapping persistent Sidebar and Topbar
context/ – AuthContext providing user state and token to the entire tree
utils/api.js – Axios instance with base URL and Authorization header injection

Authentication and user context are managed via React Context API (AuthContext) in all three frontends. Form state is handled locally using React useState in admin and owner apps, while the tenant app uses Formik + Yup for validation-heavy registration and payment forms. No Redux is used.

Each frontend maintains a centralized Axios instance (utils/api.js or services/api.js) that automatically attaches the JWT Bearer token from localStorage to every request header. API calls are made inside async functions within component useEffect hooks or event handlers.

The backend follows a RESTful MVC pattern with the following module breakdown: routes/ define URL paths, controllers/ contain business logic, models/ define Mongoose schemas, and middlewares/ handle cross-cutting concerns.

JWT tokens are issued on login with the user role embedded in the payload. The protect middleware validates the token on every protected route. The requireRole() middleware enforces role-based access control (RBAC), ensuring for example that only owners can create properties and only tenants can initiate payments.
protect – decodes and verifies JWT; attaches user object to req.user
requireRole([roles]) – checks req.user.role against allowed roles
upload (Multer) – handles multipart/form-data for property images and avatars
Express built-ins – express.json() for body parsing, cors() for cross-origin support

All controller functions are wrapped in try/catch blocks. Errors are returned as JSON objects with an appropriate HTTP status code (400 for validation, 401/403 for auth, 404 for not found, 500 for server errors). Mongoose validation errors bubble up naturally via the catch block.

Search Fields: Property title, property address (tenant portal); user name and email (admin panel)
Filtering Criteria: Property availability (available = true/false); payment status (paid / pending / failed); date range for payment history; user role (admin panel)

Implementation Approach: Frontend-side filtering is applied to data already fetched from the API using JavaScript array filter() and includes() methods. Backend query parameters (e.g., ?available=true) are supported on the properties endpoint via Mongoose query chaining.
Secure online rent payment processing between tenants and property owners
Tenant triggers initiate-payment -> server creates PaymentIntent -> client confirms with card details -> server receives webhook or client confirmation -> payment saved in MongoDB
Payment amount, status, and Stripe transaction ID are stored in the Payment collection; shown in owner and tenant payment history dashboards
Secondary External Service: SendGrid Email API
Transactional email notifications for new property listings, lease generation, and alerts
On property creation, all tenants in the database receive an automated email. On lease generation, tenant receives a confirmation email with lease details

PDF Lease Agreement Generation – pdf-lib dynamically generates a PDF contract pre-filled with tenant name, property address, rent amount, and lease dates. Stored server-side and downloadable on demand.
Email Notifications – SendGrid dispatches automated emails on key events (new listing, tenant assignment). Nodemailer is also configured as a fallback SMTP mailer.
File Upload & Avatar Management – Multer middleware processes multipart property images (up to 4 per listing) and owner avatars, storing them in the backend /public/uploads directory.
Admin Reports – The admin panel can generate and download a CSV/PDF summary report covering all platform data.

Tenant Frontend: Register, Login, Dashboard, Browse Properties (search & filter), Pay Rent (Stripe embedded form), Payment History, Lease Agreements page, AuthContext and Axios API service, form validation with Formik & Yup. Tenant Backend: tenant routes, tenant controller (initiate/confirm payment, payment history, balance), Payment model, Tenant model, Stripe integration. Admin Panel (shared): Admin Login & Password Reset page, Users Management page (view/search all users), admin getAllUsers controller and userRoutes.

Owner Frontend: Owner Login/Register, Owner Dashboard, Add/Edit Property form (image upload), My Properties table, Manage Tenants screen, Lease Agreements page (generate & download PDF), Payment History page, Profile/Avatar update, Sidebar & Topbar, AuthContext and Axios API service. Owner Backend: property routes, property controller (CRUD, add-tenant, email notifications via SendGrid), lease routes, lease controller (generate/download PDF via pdf-lib, update status), Property model, Lease model, Multer upload middleware, emailService utility. Admin Panel (shared): Dashboard page (Recharts analytics, KPI cards), Properties management table, admin dashboard controller, admin report generation.
